Rook Dispatch / Product School case study

What happened in Release 4.2

Dispatch shortened the time to answer and put more weight on proximity. Missed pings climbed. Every miss could lower a responder’s chances of getting the next offer.

Module 1 / Origin Story

4.2 changed the clock and the ranking

90 → 60 sec

Time to answer a ping

0.45 → 0.60

Weight on travel-time proximity

4.2 shipped on August 12, 2026. Dispatch gave nearby responders more weight and moved unanswered offers along sooner. Acceptance history’s weight fell from 0.40 to 0.25.

Module 1 release and handoff findings. Working context

32

Reports of pings expiring too quickly across the review period

The review covered 147 tickets and four September interviews. Three of four handlers mentioned fast-expiring callouts. Ticket totals include repeat reports, with two tickets counted in both categories.

Module 3 / Rewind

More callouts went unaccepted

Before 4.223 / 430 · 5.3%
After 4.244 / 345 · 12.8%

The count rose by 21, and that increase was entirely in callouts involving a miss. Across the same windows, ping acceptance fell from 407/525 (77.5%) to 301/482 (62.4%), and missed pings rose from 12 to 91.

Equal 21-day windows excluding release day. Module 3 analysis and responder-week rollup

Module 4 / X-Ray Vision

A miss could make the next offer less likely

Offer expires
Acceptance score falls by 0.12
Lower score can move the responder down the next ranking

The 4.2 code applies the same 0.12 deduction to a miss and an explicit decline, with no automatic recovery. In the reconstructed callout 41245, Farlight missed and her score reached 0.00. Cindermark accepted and reached 1.00. The replay assumes scores carried through release and no unlogged updates. The ping records lack candidate ranks, travel times, and delivery timestamps, so each release change’s contribution remains uncertain.

Module 5 / Recorded callouts

Farlight’s recorded misses drove her score to zero

Across 86 recorded offers, Farlight entered the release at 0.84. Seven of the 11 offers from August 12 onward expired. Replaying those same outcomes with the proposed rule leaves her at 0.76 after her last recorded offer on August 28.

Both lines start at the code’s neutral score of 0.50 and use the historical rule before August 12. The dashed line reconstructs scores from logged responses, assuming no unlogged score changes. The red line applies the proposal from the August 12 release date and removes the penalty for misses. The replay holds recorded offers and responses fixed. It estimates score changes, while future offer volume and assignment outcomes would need a trial.

Source: Rook Dispatch ping records for Farlight, June 30 to August 28, 2026. Scoring code

Module 6 / Sidekicks

The checklist makes release risks visible earlier

  1. Before approval

    Review the brief

    Check for a named owner, a success measure, consistent scope, and a problem statement before the fix. The brief passed after Helen was named to lead the walkthrough and report findings.

  2. Verify the change

    Wen checks how the change affects offer order. Ravi confirms which rank and delivery events can be captured.

  3. Rehearse the callouts

    Helen tests Accept, Miss, Decline, and no backup with the same candidates under both rules.

  4. Before launch

    Set trial criteria

    Set a target for first-offer share after a miss and regional limits for slower assignments or more unassigned callouts. Agree on when to pause or expand.

  5. First trial days

    Review signals daily

    Ravi reviews misses, first offers, and unassigned callouts. Nadia surfaces missing or fast-expiring offers so Marcus can trace affected callouts.
